solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: End of penis — ee! — on crossword solver, so long

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of penis
taken as written
the person solving the crossword is you, the reader

explanation.surface: A smutty exclamation about a body part, ending with a farewell to the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts one piece above the next, so the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: See you and so long are both casual ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: (& 4dn.) For those who want to learn how to gas dinner party intellectuals?

definitions.text: For those who want to learn how to gas
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: lessons in ..., since to gas is to talk idly
second meaning: the articulate, opinionated middle class who talk politics over dinner

explanation.surface: A sneer at self-important intellectuals who talk endlessly around the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half pretends the phrase means courses of instruction in talking; gas is slang for idle chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: The chattering classes is the derisive name for educated, opinion-voicing professionals, the type found debating at dinner parties.

clue.text: (& 7dn.) A quick shag, no lying!

parts.note: surface reading: a brief sexual encounter, and that is the honest truth
setter's reading: nobody lies down, so the act is done standing up

explanation.walkthrough: 'No lying' sounds like an assurance of honesty, but it means not lying down; shag is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang term names hurried sex while standing, which makes the legs shake.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Prominent row supporting ministerial arses?

parts.note: surface reading: a very public quarrel propping up some idiotic ministers
setter's reading: the foremost line of seats in the Commons, on which ministers sit

explanation.walkthrough: Row suggests a quarrel and arses suggests fools, but the row is a line of seats and the arses are the ministers' backsides sitting on it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the House of Commons, government ministers and their shadows occupy the foremost seats facing each other.

clue.text: Celeb arses on the rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: both are mild British exclamations of annoyance

explanation.surface: A celebrity's backside is getting more famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Arses is not the body part here but the cry of irritation, like 'damn!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeb is a celebrity, a famous person, and a star is the usual word for one.

clue.text: see 3dn.
H. Mantel's novel about love for alcohol

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round another piece
novel means new, so the letters come out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters of the novelist's initial and surname
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Hilary Mantel has written a novel about loving drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a noun for one of Hilary Mantel's books, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Methanol, or methyl alcohol, is the simplest member of the alcohol family of chemicals.

clue.text: Hit back and make flipping Brenda go off!

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina
milk that goes off turns sour

explanation.surface: Someone vows to retaliate and make that blasted Brenda explode.
explanation.walkthrough: Flipping reads as a mild curse but signals reversal; Private Eye calls the late Queen Brenda.
explanation.definitionFit: To return a ball is to hit it back to the opponent, as in tennis.

clue.text: Bush, well on right, let off

indicators.note: something off is out of order or awry, so these letters are disturbed

parts.note: both are exclamations of surprise
R is the abbreviation for right
the three letters shuffled

explanation.surface: George Bush, comfortably on the political right, was let off.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the president; it is the definition, a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers, so it is a bush.

clue.text: Broadcast transgressed against City's characteristic group of symptoms

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the words are taken by ear

parts.note: transgressed against is sinned, and the City is Rome, the Eternal City

explanation.surface: A news report says a football club offended against Manchester City.
explanation.walkthrough: City suggests Manchester City or the City of London, but here it is Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a set of symptoms that occur together and mark a particular condition.

clue.text: Dominating type, Brenda, on the buzzer

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen
a bee buzzes

explanation.surface: A bossy woman, the Queen herself, on the phone or doorbell.
explanation.walkthrough: The buzzer suggests a doorbell or intercom, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen bee is a woman who domineers over others in her circle, like the ruler of the hive.

clue.text: Brian's most agitated about right to "group-solve problems"

indicators.note: about means around, so the stirred letters surround one more
something agitated is stirred up, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Brian is furious about the right way to tackle problems as a team.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the name to the rest; the quoted definition is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainstorm is to generate ideas as a group, throwing out suggestions to solve a problem.

clue.text: Preserve spunk

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to keep fruit or vegetables in jars
second meaning: British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.walkthrough: Spunk has a cruder slang sense the clue plays on, but here it means pluck.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle fruit is to preserve it in jars, and bottle is British slang for courage or nerve.

clue.text: Little Tom's team's digital "cruncher"

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so little Tom is Thumb, with the 's kept
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A child's football side turns out to be a number-crunching computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Digital cruncher suggests a computer, but digits here are fingers and thumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbscrew was a torture device that crushed the thumbs, so it literally crunched a digit.

clue.text: (& 18ac.) Harry quiet in QI broadcast: this didn't seem to bother Tony much

definitions.text: this didn't seem to bother Tony much

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Prince Harry stays silent on the TV quiz QI, which Tony Blair shrugged off.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a BBC panel quiz; Tony is Tony Blair, who led Britain into the Iraq war and was later examined by the Chilcot inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chilcot investigation into Britain's role in the Iraq war criticised Blair, who appeared largely unrepentant.

clue.text: It's not easy with a plonker banging away

parts.note: hard is the opposite of easy
taken as written
both are British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Sex is a struggle when the partner is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: A plonker is a British idiot, as is a tit; banging away is the working-hard sense dressed up as a sexual one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard at it means working busily and continuously, just as banging away at a task does.

clue.text: see 16ac.
Sad Darling's first to go, given the boot

indicators.note: to go means to be removed, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: dejected means downcast or sad

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of Darling

explanation.surface: Alistair Darling, the dismal Chancellor, was first out of the Cabinet when sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Darling looks like Labour's Alistair Darling; it only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ejected is to be thrown out, which is what getting the boot means.

clue.text: Peter Jones possibly wearing Deborah's clothes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Peter Jones is an investor on the TV show ...' Den
second meaning, split in two: in women's clothing (drag) and wearing it (on)

explanation.surface: Is businessman Peter Jones going about in a woman's outfit?
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Jones is also a London department store, but here he is the tall entrepreneur; Deborah just stands for any woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The investors on Dragons' Den are called dragons, and a man in drag has women's clothes on.

clue.text: Major load of bollocks as a national symbol?

parts.note: John Major, the former prime minister
bull is slang for nonsense, as is bollocks

explanation.surface: A complaint that some major nonsense is being passed off as a patriotic emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: Major looks like an adjective meaning big; it is the prime minister John Major.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bull is the stout cartoon figure who personifies England, much as Uncle Sam does America.

clue.text: The one French Conservative hot crafty thing

parts.note: la is the feminine 'the' in French
un is French for one
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A French Tory is described as sexy and sly.
explanation.walkthrough: French governs both the and one; crafty thing means a type of craft, not a cunning person.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is a motor boat, and boats are craft, so it is a playful 'crafty thing'.

clue.text: Pop article about sex — cold and sad

parts.note: pop and pa both mean father
the definite article

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the following word is read backwards

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A tabloid pop-music piece about sex is unfeeling and dismal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop article suggests a piece about pop music; pop is father and article is the word the.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic in its casual sense means pitiful or sad.

clue.text: (& 25dn.) Unwanted post: Head of Anti-prejudice involved with the Tory rag

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are entwined into a new order
the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Anti-prejudice
taken as written
the Daily Mail is a right-wing tabloid

explanation.surface: An anti-racism campaigner gets nasty letters linked to the Daily Mail.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a contemptuous word for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate mail is abusive letters sent to someone, the sort of post nobody wants to receive.

clue.text: Muff filth all over

parts.note: muck is dirt or filth
when time is up, it is all over

explanation.surface: A crude remark about dirt spread over a woman's genitals.
explanation.walkthrough: Muff looks like the vulgar noun, but it is the verb meaning to fumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To muff a catch or a chance is to bungle it, which is what mucking up means.

clue.text: see 24dn.
Snicker supplier of Bristol?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, comic: something that provides tits, since Bristols is rhyming slang for breasts

explanation.walkthrough: Bristol looks like the city; in rhyming slang Bristol City means titty, so a supplier of one is a 'titter'.
explanation.definitionFit: To titter is to giggle nervously, the same suppressed laugh as a snicker.

clue.text: Superior quality of Brit artist wanting money without pressure

parts.note: Tracey Emin, one of the Young British Artists

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: pence are British coins
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A British artist is short of cash despite her quality.
explanation.walkthrough: Wanting means lacking in the surface, but here it just links artist to the money; Tracey Emin made the unmade bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is distinction or high standing, being superior to others.
